items.question: Which method best helps you learn about hot and cold?
options: Observe or use evidence, connect it to the concept, and explain the conclusion.

items.question: Explain hot and cold and give one everyday example.
items.answer: A strong answer gives an accurate explanation and a relevant example.

items.question: Apply hot and cold to a new everyday situation. What would you observe or use as evidence?
items.expected_response: Relevant evidence followed by a reasoned conclusion.

items.question: What best demonstrates mastery of 'Temperature and its Measurement'?
options: Use major ideas independently in a new situation and explain the reasoning.
Finish the lesson without checking understanding.

items.answer: A defensible answer that identifies a foundational idea and teaches it accurately.

flashcards.back: Define hot and cold, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define temperature, give an example, and explain why it matters.
Define thermometer, give an example, and explain why it matters.

interactive_activities.title: Explore hot and cold
interactive_activities.instructions: Use a safe, age-appropriate task specifically focused on hot and cold. Record what you notice, explain it, and state what you learned.

interactive_activities.title: Use it in a new situation
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a new situation where temperature is useful and explain your reasoning.

interactive_activities.title: Teach it back
interactive_activities.instructions: Teach measurement and safety to a beginner in 3–5 clear steps.
